subject: Post-demo synthesis: model evaluation criteria, prompt sets, and mitigation plan
body:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@clearlane.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo synthesis: model evaluation criteria, prompt sets, and mitigation plan

Emily — thanks again for your time today. Quick synthesis and proposed next steps from our end so we can move into a short evaluation sprint: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: extract structured billing codes and short clinical rationale from free-text visit notes (latency sensitive for near-real-time UX in the clinician workflow).
- High tolerance for slightly higher latency if accuracy (macro-level code F1) and hallucination controls are strong.
- You have an internal proprietary classifier used as a baseline; primary ask is to understand whether an open model can match or exceed that baseline on precision for critical codes.

Proposed evaluation scope (2-week sprint)
1) Model candidates: run two families — a high-capacity open LLM (quantized gpt-open-ggml variant) and a tuned mid-size open LLM (instruction-tuned, 8-bit). We'll also include your proprietary baseline as an oracle for parity checks.
2) Metrics: code-level precision/recall/F1 per code bucket, hallucination rate (measured via hallucination checklist in prompt tests), and regression delta vs baseline across your acceptance prompt set.
3) Acceptance thresholds: primary: macro F1 >= baseline - 0.02 (2 percentage points). Safety: hallucination incidents <= baseline + 0.5%. Latency: p95 inference <= 850ms (on dedicated capacity profile).
4) Artifacts we will deliver: recommended prompt bundles, a reproducible eval harness (notebook + CSV), and a short mitigation playbook with fallback routing to baseline when confidence is low.

Attachments: I uploaded the prompt bundle we discussed and a starter benchmark CSV (see attachments).

Next steps / asks for you
- Emily: share a 200–500 note sample (anonymized) and the output schema for mapping codes.
- Jordan: confirm whether we can run an evaluation job in your staging VPC (preferred) or if you need us to run on Redwood dedicated and share artifacts.

Kickoff: if you share the sample by Thu 9/10 we can deliver initial comparisons by Thu 9/24.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate scheduling for a 30-min technical walkthrough with Karthik and Connor if that timeline works.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

- Baseline stats: our proprietary classifier currently reports macro F1 0.82 on the production holdout. Latency is ~420ms p95 in our internal infra.
- We want the open-model candidate to at minimum match precision on high-risk codes (heart attack, stroke, anticoagulation). Those are the ones where false positives cause treatment delays.

We can provide the anonymized sample by Thursday. Regarding environment: Jordan is out most of this week but I’ll check if staging VPC access is an option; otherwise Redwood running the job in Dedicated and sharing artifacts is fine.

Also please include any prompt-level safety checks you plan to run — we want to see how hallucinations are being identified.

—Emily

Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: model evaluation criteria, prompt sets, and mitigation plan

Hi Emily — thanks for the baseline numbers, that helps. A few technical notes and links to the artifacts we referenced: 

1) Benchmarks and harness
- I pushed a starter harness to the shared Drive (link below). It contains the evaluation script, basic scoring, and a sample prompt bundle. The benchmark CSV in attachments is a formatted example with columns for input_id, note_text, baseline_label, baseline_confidence, expected_schema.
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-eval-benchmarks

2) Prompt sets and safety checks
- Prompt set: prompt_bundles/clearlane_v1.json — included as attachment "; clearlane_eval_promptset_v1.json (application/json)". It contains: (a) canonical extraction prompt, (b) a forced-output schema template, (c) two negative tests to surface hallucinations, (d) a confidence calibration probe.
- Safety checks: we flag outputs that: 1) produce tokens outside the schema, 2) list codes not present in the note, or 3) have low-confidence tokens according to the model's scoring head. We mark those for human review and route to your baseline classifier if policy dictates.

3) Model variants to try
- Open-large-q8: 34B open model, 8-bit quantized (higher accuracy, higher p95).
- Open-mid-tuned: 11B instruction-tuned variant (lower cost, faster).
- We will run both and compute per-code deltas vs your baseline. We’ll also compute a weighted-score where high-risk codes have 3x weight.

4) Acceptance table (quick summary)
- Macro F1: candidate >= baseline - 0.02
- High-risk code precision: candidate >= baseline
- Hallucination incidents: candidate <= baseline + 0.5%
- Rollback policy: if weighted-score < baseline by 0.03, route to baseline and mark as not accepted for that cohort.

I attached an export of the starter benchmark (openmodel_bench_v2.csv). We’ll iterate on the prompt bundle after we see the sample.

Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: model evaluation criteria, prompt sets, and mitigation plan

Hi team — quick note on operational safeguards and rollout options that tie into the acceptance thresholds Karthik outlined: 

- Canary routing: we can route X% of traffic to the open-model candidate with real-time scoring and fallback to your baseline on low-confidence outputs. Canary can be region-bounded and limited by per-code cohorts.
- Traceability: the harness can emit a short explainability object (top-3 contributing prompt tokens + confidence) per record and an audited decision log with request id. That output is a small JSON per record, retained per your retention policy.
- Rollback & SLA: if the open candidate’s weighted-score drops below baseline by > 0.03 for 24 hours, we trigger automatic rollback to baseline for that cohort and create a high-priority incident ticket.

Operational ask: if you prefer Redwood-hosted Dedicated runs we’ll sign the standard data processing addendum and provide an S3 bucket per project with configurable retention. If you need staging VPC access, we’ll share a deployment manifest and run the jobs inside your environment.

—Connor
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@clearlane.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.cto@clearlane.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo synthesis: model evaluation criteria, prompt sets, and mitigation plan

Emily / Jordan — answering both points together:

- Hallucination incident: any output that assigns a code that is not supported by the note text or that fabricates a clinical assertion used to justify a code (e.g., system adds "STEMI" when the note describes "chest pain pending labs"). Our negative tests in the prompt bundle are designed to surface these. We’ll include concrete examples in the report.
- Tradeoffs: we do not recommend allowing higher hallucination in exchange for precision on high-risk codes. Safety-first for those cohorts. If there is a low-risk cohort where precision improvements materially help downstream metrics, we can explore a controlled tolerance window, but that is a separate scope item.

Also attaching the parity acceptance quick-sheet (parity_acceptance_table.xlsx) and the prompt set (clearlane_eval_promptset_v1.json).

Vanessa

This is helpful. We’ll send the anonymized sample by EOD Thursday and confirm staging VPC availability early next week. A couple remaining items for clarity before the sprint:

- Can you confirm what fallback latency looks like when routing to baseline (we need to ensure clinician UX is acceptable)?
- Will Redwood include a short runbook for human-in-the-loop triage for flagged hallucination incidents?

Appreciate the clarity — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Emily


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@clearlane.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700

Emily — quick answers to your final two asks:

- Fallback latency: typical routing to your baseline classifier adds ~120–250ms depending on the cohort and network path; we’ll include p95 numbers in the onboarding doc and can run a short ping test as part of the staging run.
- Runbook: yes — we’ll deliver a short human-in-the-loop runbook that describes triage (inspect explainability trace, curator verification, escalate to clinical SME), sample templates for labeling, and an incident checklist.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min technical kickoff Tuesday 9/15 10am PT (tentative).

Thanks — Vanessa
